title: One-day miniroll pocket slate & operator microflow (May 2026)
content:
Context:
This is a compact day-of-run pocket slate for small, low-risk launches where we want a one-day push with fast rollback lanes. The focus is: short window, tight telemetry sampling, quick comms, and an operator microflow that a single deploy conductor can run.

High level goals:
- keep blast radius minimal (1–2 services max)
- collect precise latency & error samples at 1-min cadence for first 60 minutes
- auto-fallback to safe model variant / previous image on anomaly triggers
- post-launch smoke checklist completed within 2 hours

Before launch (T-48h to T-1h):
- [ ] Finalize change list and owner per service (owner tags in JIRA RE-4721)
- [ ] Run quick dependency graph: confirm no infra upgrades landing during window
- [ ] Bake canary image + checksum, push to canary repo (tag: canary-2026-05-XX)
- [ ] Pre-snapshot telemetry: capture baseline 24h pre-launch (latency p50/p95/p99, token QPS, error-rate)
- [ ] Alerting rules smoke: ensure mute windows outside operator channel
- [ ] Communication: schedule 1h pre-call with on-call + product PM + solutions engineer

Day-of timeline (compact):
- T-60m: pre-call, quick rundown of rollback plan, confirm runbook link
- T-30m: dry-run of canary rollout script against staging; verify metrics pipeline ingest
- T-10m: set Slack channel to silent except ops conductor and incident leads
- T+0m: start canary at 1% traffic; record timestamp and canary tag
- T+5m: telemetry sanity (service up, traces flowing, no obvious errors)
- T+15m: if stable, step canary to 10%
- T+30m: if stable, step canary to 50%
- T+45m: if stable, step canary to 100% and mark release as promoted
- T+60m: full smoke, soak checks, add release note stub to Confluence

Operator microflow (scriptable checklist):
1) Lock release note template and create stub: title, changelog bullets, owner
2) Pull canary artifact + verify checksum (sha256)
3) Trigger canary route change via router API (curl + auth) and record approval id
4) Start telemetry sampler (run script: tools/tele-sampler.sh --qps 100 --window 60s --metrics latency,error)
5) After each step, call out status in #release-ops: "step: X; status: OK/FAIL; note"
6) If any step FAILS, immediately run fallback script: tools/fallback.sh --target previous-tag --force --notify

Telemetry & gating (concrete thresholds):
- latency: p99 increase > 2x baseline over a sliding 5-min window -> FAIL
- error-rate: 5xx spike > 0.5% absolute or > 3x baseline -> FAIL
- user-visible: elevated 4xx rate + support tickets opened in first 30m -> FAIL
- infra: pod restart rate > 2/min or node OOMs -> FAIL
Notes: thresholds can be tuned by service; keep public-facing services conservative.

Communication templates (shortcuts):
- Pre-call announcement: "H: Launch pre-call at T-60. Owners: Dana K, Marco R. Canaries: svc-a:v3-canary. Rollback plan: RE-4721. Channel: #release-ops."
- Promote announcement: "PROMOTE: canary-tag canary-2026-05-XX promoted to 100% at T+45 by @DanaK. Release notes: confluence://release-notes/miniroll-2026-05 (stub)."
- Rollback alert (auto): "ROLLBACK TRIGGERED by telemetry gate. Initiated fallback to svc-a:v2 at T+XX. Incident lead: @LeahO."

Quick rollback matrix (one-line):
- code regression (errors/latency) -> revert to previous image tag (tools/fallback.sh)
- infra instability -> scale down canary + set traffic to regionally isolated nodes -> require SRE clearance
- configuration bug -> flip feature flag off (flags-service UI) and prune config caches

Post-launch (T+2h to T+72h):
- [ ] Post-smoke signoff from QA and SRE (T+2h)
- [ ] Fill release note details: impact, rollout timeline, reverted changes (if any)
- [ ] Schedule 48h retrospective if any gates tripped (owner = Marco Ruiz)
- [ ] Telemetry retention: snapshot first 2h at 1-min cadence, 48h at 5-min cadence

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who is the primary on-call for infra-side rollbacks if node-level problems appear? (SRE rota unclear for holiday week)
- Decide whether to include client-side feature flag ramp for mobile vs web in the same rollout or separate minirolls
- Automate the canary promotion approval step (existing API is manual; short-term keep manual to retain human judgment)

Handy command snippets (for operator):
- Promote to 10%: curl -X POST https://router.redwood.ai/api/route --data '{"svc":"svc-a","percent":10,"tag":"canary-2026-05-XX"}' --header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Telemetry sampler: ./tools/tele-sampler.sh --service svc-a --qps 200 --window 60 --metrics p50,p95,p99,errors
- Fallback: ./tools/fallback.sh --service svc-a --tag svc-a:v2 --reason "telemetry-trigger"

Short retro prompts (if anything non-trivial):
- What signal best predicted the issue? (latency, errors, infra)
- Which step took longest and why? (manual approvals, slow metric ingest)
- What can be automated without increasing risk? (promote approvals, one-click fallback)

Notes to self:
- Keep the doc lean; operators don't want a 20-page manual for minirolls.
- Cross-link to full release runbook for heavyweight launches (confluence://release-runbook/full-scale)
- If we run this twice in a week, propose a tiny automation project to reduce manual promote time from 4m to <60s.

-- Dana K (draft)
